name: Hanun
title: King of Ammon who dishonored David's envoys
summary: Hanun was the son of Nahash and became king over the Ammonites after his father's death. He is best known for having dishonored David's envoys by shaving off half of their beards and cutting their garments, which led to war between Israel and Ammon. His poor counsel and lack of diplomatic wisdom resulted in a devastating defeat for the Ammonites.

keyEvents.title: Hanun becomes king over Ammon
keyEvents.description: After King Nahash of Ammon died, his son Hanun succeeded him to the throne.

keyEvents.title: David sends envoys to show sympathy
keyEvents.description: David sent servants to Hanun to comfort him after his father's death, because Nahash had shown kindness to David.

keyEvents.title: Hanun dishonors David's envoys
keyEvents.description: Following advice from his princes, Hanun suspected the envoys of being spies. He shaved off half of their beards and cut their garments at the hips, sending them away in disgrace.

keyEvents.title: The Ammonites prepare for war
keyEvents.description: When Hanun realized he had made himself hated by David, he hired Syrian soldiers to fight against Israel.

keyEvents.title: Israel defeats the Ammonites and their allies
keyEvents.description: Joab led the army of Israel and defeated both the Ammonites and the Syrian mercenaries in a decisive battle.

keyEvents.title: The Conquest of Rabbah
keyEvents.description: David and Joab besieged and captured Rabbah, the capital of the Ammonites, marking the final defeat of Hanun's kingdom.
